summary: The narrator and his parents visit Ron Glover, Darryl's father, in his messy apartment to tell him that Darryl is alive and held prisoner on Treasure Island. Ron, shaken, shaves, dresses in a military uniform, and joins them on a midnight drive down the 101 to Mountain View to see Barbara Stratford, an investigative reporter for the Bay Guardian whom the family knows. The passage ends as Mom has phoned Barbara ahead of the visit.
one_line: Narrator and parents tell Darryl's father that Darryl is alive on Treasure Island, then drive to reporter Barbara Stratford.
key_facts: Darryl's father, Ron Glover, is in a messy house with greasy food-trays and dented sofa cushions when the narrator's group arrives.
Ron Glover moves sheets off the sofa and carries stacked food-trays into the kitchen before sitting down with the group.
The narrator tells Ron that "Darryl is alive and being held prisoner on Treasure Island."
Ron stuffs his fist in his mouth and makes a horrible groaning sound on hearing the news.
The narrator's father says the family has a friend who "writes for the Bay Guardian" and is "An investigative reporter."
Barbara Stratford had been at the free weekly Bay Guardian for a long time, while many reporters had left for bigger dailies and the Internet.
Mom asks Ron Glover, "Will you tell her Darryl's story?"
Ron Glover shakes off the narrator's father's hand when Dad tries to comfort him.
Ron Glover returns downstairs having shaved, gelled his hair back, and put on a crisp military dress uniform with campaign ribbons.
Ron Glover smells a little of beer, which seems to be coming through his pores.
The group arrives at Barbara Stratford's driveway at midnight.
Barbara Stratford lives out of town in Mountain View, reached by driving down the 101.
The narrator describes the Mountain View area as a different Bay Area, with high-tech buildings, freeways and subdivisions of identical houses.
Mom had phoned Barbara before the group arrived.
